title: SE Enablement: Messaging + Competitive Demo Practice
summary: Internal SE enablement focused on sharpening messaging and demo flow for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployments. Practiced two demo segments with live role-play, surfaced common objections (latency, cost, data residency), and aligned on collateral updates and follow-up role-play session.

Sofia to send competitor battlecard and pricing quick sheet by 2027-11-22
Lina to update two slides on Dedicated sizing and fallback policies by 2027-11-25

Sofia Patel: Share competitor battlecard (OpenAI/Anthropic/Vertex) and one-pager on cost levers - due 2027-11-22
Lina Gomez: Update product slides (autoscaling, KV cache mention, fallback policies) - due 2027-11-25

transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Sofia, Marco, Lina, Emma, Dev, Taylor

Summary: quick internal SE enablement; practice messaging and demo with competitive framing and objection handling.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, I think we can go ahead and get started. Thanks for carving out the hour. We'll do a quick agenda  messaging refresher, two short demo runs, and then role-play/objections. Marco, you wanna kick us off?

[00:22] Marco: Yeah, sure. Good afternoon all. I'll start with the high-level messaging. Remember our four pillars for customers: latency, cost, reliability, and deployment flexibility. We call it the L-C-R-D framework  latency, cost, reliability, deployment. Might be a mouthful, but it helps.

[00:45] Lina: Quick note  when you say deployment flexibility, mention dedicated vs hosted vs private explicitly; customers latch onto those terms.

[01:10] Marco: Right. So, example opener: "We help teams ship LLM features with consistent performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments  so you can choose the right tradeoffs for latency, cost, and compliance." Does that land?

[01:30] Dev: I like it, but maybe call out fallback policies earlier  customers worry about degradations.

[01:45] Marco: Good shout. I'll add a short line about automated fallbacks to compatible variants and region routing.

[02:10] Emma: Also add a short sentence on observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns, tracing, rollouts. People want to know they can measure regressions.

[02:35] Sofia: Perfect. Okay demo plan  we'll run Demo A: Hosted API flow focusing on fast onboarding and streaming responses, then Demo B: Dedicated capacity with autoscaling and predictable throughput. Each demo ~10 minutes. I'll role-play as prospect for the first run. Marco demo leads.

[03:00] Marco: Sounds good. Launching the Hosted demo... loading the quickstart. Note, the transcript might be a bit messy cause I'm talking while typing.

[03:30] [demo noises / keyboard] Marco: Ok, here we call the generation endpoint  streaming responses come back in 200-300 ms per chunk in this local test. Mention the model catalog and Redwood-verified profiles.

[04:05] Taylor (interrupting): Quick Q  how do you explain price differences between hosted and dedicated?

[04:15] Marco: Good question. We frame it as: hosted for fastest time-to-value and lower initial commitment, dedicated for predictable unit economics when you have sustained throughput. Then list levers  batching, quantization, KV/prefix caching.

[04:40] Emma: Make sure reps have a one-liner: "If you're sensitive to per-token cost at scale, we typically recommend Dedicated with intelligent batching and cache profiles  you get 20-40% unit savings depending on workload." Numbers are illustrative, call out that we have Optimize tooling.

[05:10] Marco: Yep, I said that, mention Redwood Optimize. Also that the runtime picks kernels and compiles per-model to squeeze latency. Might be too techy, but useful for SEs.

[05:35] Sofia: Okay let's run the first role-play. I'll be a Product Manager at a fintech with PII concerns. Marco you demo Hosted but anticipate a privacy question.

[05:50] [role-play start]
[06:00] Sofia (PM): We process sensitive documents; what guarantees do you have for data residency and retention?

[06:12] Marco: We offer Private deployments and VPC/on-prem options. For Hosted we can do retention controls, but for regulated workloads we recommend Private with customer-managed networking and KMS.

[06:30] Sofia: And what about audits  SOC2, ISO?

[06:35] Marco: We have SOC2 in progress and mature audit logs in the Console. We do RBAC and SSO integrations  SAML etc.

[06:50] Sofia: Ok good. That felt pretty natural. Couple of notes: avoid saying "we have SOC2 in progress" as a standalone  say the expected timeline or link to the compliance packet.

[07:10] Lina: Also mention optional HSM/KMS integrations for key management  customers want detail.

[07:30] Marco: Noted. Quick feedback  my wording on "Private is for regulated workloads" maybe too binary. We should say "for workloads requiring strict network isolation or residency, Private is recommended, otherwise Dedicated offers isolation and predictable throughput with a lower ops footprint."

[07:55] Sofia: Nice. Ok, Demo B  Dedicated. Marco switch to the dedicated dashboard and show autoscaling rules and reserved GPU pools.

[08:20] Marco: Loading Dedicated console. Here you can pin model versions, configure autoscaling policies and burst capacity, set SLOs. Call out canary rollouts and fallback policies in case a model variant degrades.

[08:50] Dev: How granular can autoscaling be? customers often ask about minute-level vs hour-level.

[09:00] Marco: Right now our autoscaling supports minute-level scaling with configurable cooldowns; we also support burst policies for sudden spikes.

[09:20] Taylor: Another standard objection: latency for long-context models  how do we position Redwood?

[09:28] Marco: We talk about smart routing, KV cache, continuous batching, and compilation/kernel selection. For long context we emphasize KV cache and model variants tuned for long tokens; sometimes a trimmed seq length variant is better.

[09:55] Emma: Make sure you don't overload the buyer with "kernel selection"  keep it as "engine optimizations for latency on GPU" unless you have a deep SE.

[10:15] Marco: Good. We'll keep the deep detail for technical deep dives.

[10:30] [role-play  Dedicated objection]
[10:40] Sofia (CISO role): We already invested in internal infra; why not just self-host?

[10:50] Marco: That's common. We position Redwood as a way to avoid reinventing inference ops  our runtime and orchestration layer handles continuous batching, KV cache management, and model rollouts. If they want full self-host, we compare operational cost and time-to-market. Also mention our Private package for air-gapped or on-prem scenarios.

[11:15] Sofia: They might ask for a benchmark  what do we offer?

[11:22] Marco: We can run a short POC with representative prompts  we offer benchmark spreadsheets and can run latency/cost per-token comparisons. Suggest tracking latency p50/p95 and per-token cost in the spreadsheet.

[11:40] Lina: Note: bring the benchmark template link in follow-up  reps love a ready-to-fill sheet.

[12:00] Marco: Alright third segment: competitive framing  quick lines.

[12:10] Marco: Against OpenAI: emphasize deployment flexibility and on-prem/private options, plus model catalog and cost controls. Against Anthropic: highlight unified runtime and observability; also cost levers. Against cloud providers (Vertex): highlight inference optimizations and pre-tuned quantization profiles and cost-focused Optimize tooling.

[12:45] Dev: Competitors will lead with model quality and brand. We should not argue on raw samples; instead focus on economic and operational ROI.

[13:00] Taylor: Can we practice a quick objection? I'll play buyer pushing on cost  "We can get cheaper spot GPUs ourselves."

[13:12] Emma: Good one. Marco respond.

[13:20] Marco: Yeah, so, we say: if you can invest in infra and ops, you might match unit cost, but you own the engineering and maintenance. Redwood gives you a predictable SLA, rollout tooling, and a single API across hosted/dedicated/private  fewer integration costs and faster iteration. Also call out Optimize recommendations which can reduce unit cost without sacrificing accuracy.

[13:50] Sofia: Add a line about measurable cost savings we can show from prior customers (percent ranges)  use specific right-sized examples in playbooks.

[14:10] [demo practice  timed run 10m]

[14:20] Marco: Starting a condensed end-to-end demo  ingestion, embeddings, generation, streaming, then a quick reranking example.

[15:00] Marco: One caveat  when I show embeddings, the rep should mention offline batch and real-time options and how Redwood supports both.

[15:30] Taylor: Quick technical callout: how do we explain quantization? reps often say "we do 4-bit quantization; will that break quality?"

[15:45] Marco: Keep it simple: Quantization reduces memory and can slightly affect llm quality; we recommend profiling to pick the right quantization profile per workload and Redwood's runtime supports several quantized variants. Offer to run a quality regression as part of the POC.

[16:10] Emma: Good  add that to the playbook line: "offer a quantization quality regression in POC".

[16:30] [role-play  final wrap Q&A]

[16:45] Dev: Also remember to surface the Console features: token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and regression alerts tied to eval sets.

[17:05] Marco: Quick question for Lina  are we adding a slide on fallback policies in the default deck? I always forget to show that.

[17:15] Lina: Not in the default yet; I'll add a small box on the blueprint slide about fallback to variant models and region routing.

[17:35] Sofia: Ok let's run a short cold start objection  buyer says "We need on-prem, but we don't want vendor control plane."

[17:50] Marco: Response: we have Private with customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package for air-gapped deployments; we can sign an enterprise contract with support SLAs and an install runbook.

[18:10] Sofia: That felt solid. A few general coaching points: 1) avoid too many infra buzzwords early; 2) lead with business outcomes (time-to-market, units saved, reliability); 3) have playbook-ready numbers for common verticals (fintech, healthcare).

[18:40] Taylor: Can we tighten the demo transitions  sometimes it feels like a monologue. Maybe add a 10-second recap slide between major flows.

[19:00] Marco: Will do. Also, I'm going to trim the kernel selection bit unless we have a technical buyer.

[19:20] Emma: For battlecards, include one-liners vs each competitor and a 2-line rebuttal.

[19:35] Sofia: Great. Let's do final role-play: Sofia as buyer asking for pricing. Marco, keep it non-committal but helpful.

[19:50] [role-play  pricing ask]

[20:00] Sofia (Buyer): What does pricing look like for a pilot with 100k tokens/day?

[20:12] Marco: For hosted, we give a ballpark per-token plus overage; for dedicated you'd look at a reserved capacity commit with a monthly fee plus lower per-token. We usually say we need to scope the workload  batch vs real-time, average tokens per request  to provide an accurate estimate. Offer a pilot with defined SLOs and a short benchmark run.

[20:35] Dev: Call out that reps should not give exact numbers unless they consult pricing. Use ranges and offer to follow-up with pricing sheet.

[21:00] Sofia: Perfect. Ok last 30 minutes we did two runs; let's capture feedback and finalize next steps. Marco, any notes on the demo artifacts?

[21:15] Marco: I'll update the demo script to include: short compliance line, fallback policy mention, and the cost-savings one-liner. Share a recording and the demo VM link.

[21:35] Lina: I'll update slides: add fallback policy box, two bullets on Dedicated sizing, and a playbook example for quantization/regression.

[21:50] Emma: I'll schedule the follow-up role-play and invite 6 reps for practice.

[22:05] Sofia: Ok recap of next steps: Marco update script by 11/24; Sofia to send competitor battlecard by 11/22; Lina update slides by 11/25; Emma schedule follow-up by 11/23.

[22:25] Sofia: Anything else?

[22:33] Taylor: One last ask  can we have one short one-pager that summarises Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private in plain English? It's helpful for early discovery.

[22:45] Lina: I'll draft that as part of slide updates.

[23:00] Sofia: Great. Thanks everyone  meeting adjourned.

[23:10] [end meeting]

Note on transcript: Some words and product names may be transcribed slightly off (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes split as K-V, "Dedicated" pronounced "Dedicat" in a few spots). This is an internal practice recording  use for training only.
